blocks.title: Cukier
blocks.lede: One construction rule. Multiple scales. No separate logo for every problem.

items.label: Role
items.value: Logotype design, identity system, packaging, interior applications

items.label: Scope
items.value: Logotype, construction system, identity, packaging, interior

blocks.statement: The logo had three very different jobs.
body: Small packaging. Interior scale. Digital applications.

A mark that works beautifully on a label can fall apart when enlarged. A mark designed for a wall can lose its character when reduced to a few centimetres. Production adds another problem: each application may be made by a different process, by different people.

blocks.statement: Build the mark around one construction rule, then make the rule the system.
body: Instead of drawing exceptions for every format, each application becomes a variation of the same underlying logic.

blocks.text: One construction rule instead of ten versions of a logo.

body: A documented logotype construction, identity system, packaging and interior applications built from the same foundation.
The mark holds its form from small packaging to architectural scale without needing a separate redraw for every condition.
The wider point is production reality: the identity is designed to keep working even when the original designer isn’t there to check every output.
